::: {#def-npsem-ne .theorem}
## Random network NPSEM \[RNNPSEM\]

An RNNPSEM is an [NPSEM](#def-npsem) whose equations are of two kinds. *Structural* equations represent constructs measured on each [observational unit](#def-observational-unit); *relational* equations represent the causal processes linking constructs across observational units. A typical equation of each kind is

$$
\begin{aligned}
X_{ki} &= f_{X_{ki}}\big(\mathbf{Pa}(X_{ki}),\, U_{X_{ki}}\big), & X_{ki} &\in \mathscr{O}_i,\\
\psi(i,j) &= f_{\psi_{ij}}\big(\mathbf{Pa}(\psi(i,j)),\, U_{\psi_{ij}}\big), & i &\ne j.
\end{aligned}
$$

Its random variables are the observational units together with the relational variables:

$$
\mathbf V = \Big[\,\bigcup_{i \in \mathcal N} \mathscr{O}_i\Big] \cup \Big[\,\bigcup_{i,j \in \mathcal N,\ i \ne j} \psi(i,j)\Big].
$$

A **graph generator** is the matrix of relational variables, one for each ordered pair of distinct nodes, that gives the entries of a random [network graph](#def-graph):

$$
\boldsymbol\psi = \begin{bmatrix}
0 & \psi(1,2) & \cdots & \psi(1,n)\\
\psi(2,1) & 0 & \cdots & \psi(2,n)\\
\vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\
\psi(n,1) & \psi(n,2) & \cdots & 0
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Its $i$th row is the vector of [network weights](#def-graph) $\boldsymbol\Psi_i$ of unit $i$. When there are several, for example over time, they are written $\boldsymbol\psi_1, \dots, \boldsymbol\psi_T$.
:::
